title: The nine fact tables are defined in a data lake; the target has no data lake
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Reporting and Analytics Data Model v3.xlsx
section: Facts (note A2 and the Refresh column)
description: Version 3 defines the nine fact tables as a star schema in the data lake for Power BI and states that no source system is loaded directly. Arch v5 removes the data lake and the Power BI feed (INT-19 and INT-20) and gives rwb-reporting its own read model built from the business events, so the landing place of every fact table, the load and the consumer change.
evidence: v3 Facts!A2 (Star schema in the data lake for Power BI); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 line 37 and line 67 (no data lake connection; INT-19 and INT-20 removed), lines 664 to 665 (slide 37: Data lake / Power BI not connected), lines 1096 to 1119 (slide 41: P9 owns measures, snapshots, steering dashboard and regulatory reports in rwb_reporting), line 2296 (measures 01:30 from its own projections: no data lake), lines 2988 to 2990 (slide 44 JOB-15 reporting extract); ADR-018; DP-17.
proposed: The star schema is the read model in rwb_reporting (P9), fed from the service topics; the steering dashboard and the reports are served through GET /dashboards/{id} and GET /reports/{id} behind gateway-bff and no lake or Power BI connection is rebuilt.

title: The reporting layer reads recovery.v_ace_* views directly
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Reporting and Analytics Data Model v3.xlsx
description: Six refresh cells and two dimension rows take ACE rows straight from recovery.v_ace_* views into the reporting layer (account, plan, lawsuit, hearing, asset, npa asset, payment, write-off, holiday, product and bucket log). Arch v5 says only rwb-source-data reads the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views and every other service reads ACE through its contract, so the reporting layer holds no view grant and must be fed by the P1 snapshot(page) activity.
evidence: v3 Facts!F5, F7, F8, F9, F11 and F13 (Read through v_ace_*); v3 Dimensions!B5 and B6 (holidays read through v_ace_holiday; product codes read through v_ace_product); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 line 707 (only rwb-source-data reads the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views) and lines 1114 to 1119 (P1 snapshot(page) activity; P9 Temporal Source data: snapshot(page) for measures); ADR-010; DP-05.
proposed: Every ACE-fed fact and dimension takes its rows from the rwb-source-data contract and its snapshot(page) activity; the read model holds no recovery.v_ace_* grant and P9 never reads the ACE views directly.

title: The refresh wording has no schedule in the target
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Reporting and Analytics Data Model v3.xlsx
description: Version 3 describes the Workbench-side facts as loaded nightly from the Workbench and the bucket flow fact as monthly. The target runs no nightly Workbench load: the facts are event-fed projections and the measures publish at 01:30 as JOB-15, triggered by Airflow, with a hold when the dashboard count does not reconcile to the case list.
evidence: v3 Facts!F6, F10, F12 and F13 (Nightly from the Workbench; monthly); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 line 2296 (measures 01:30 in rwb-reporting from its own projections), lines 2327 to 2330 (JOB-15 at 01:30, rerun any business date, POST /reports/{id}/run) and line 2990 (JOB-15 Airflow trigger, no data lake); LDM v8 fields DF-RPT-053 to DF-RPT-058 (measure_publish status, counts and held_reason); ADR-018.
proposed: Each refresh cell reads event-fed projections with the 01:30 publish (JOB-15) and, for a rebuild, a rerun for any business date; the measure_publish row decides whether the day is published or held.

title: No fact, dimension or measure carries an owner or a schema
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Reporting and Analytics Data Model v3.xlsx
description: Version 3 names no service, no schema and no owner for any of the nine fact tables, eight dimensions and ten measures, and gives no schema for the star schema itself. The target puts the whole read model in the P9 own schema rwb_reporting and takes every input from an owning service.
evidence: v3 Facts (all rows), Dimensions (all rows) and Measures (all rows) carry no owner column and no schema; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 sheet Services row P9 (rwb-reporting, schema rwb_reporting, REST base /api/recovery/reporting/v1) and sheet Tables rows measure_definition, measure_snapshot and measure_publish (P9); Template and Rules R4 and R5.5 DP-01; ADR-014.
proposed: Owner and Values from columns are added to Facts and Dimensions and an Owner column to Measures, every value taken from the Ownership Map.

title: The read-model control tables and the queue measures are absent
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Reporting and Analytics Data Model v3.xlsx
description: Version 3 holds the measure formulas only as text and names no table for the definitions, the frozen values or the publish decision, so nothing in the model holds the version of a measure, the value frozen for a business date, or the hold when the dashboard does not reconcile to the case list. The queue measures that P3 publishes to the case list and Power BI have no row at all.
evidence: v3 Measures (ten measures, formula and fact table only); LDM v8 entities measure_definition, measure_snapshot and measure_publish (Reporting, DP03 and RPT) with fields DF-RPT-031 to DF-RPT-058, and queue_measure with fields DF-RPT-020 to DF-RPT-030; Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables rows measure_definition, measure_snapshot and measure_publish (P9) and queue_measure (P3); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 line 1096 (P9 writes measures, snapshots, steering dashboard, regulatory reports).
proposed: A Read-model controls section names measure_definition, measure_snapshot and measure_publish under P9 with the publish gate, and states that queue measures stay with P3 rwb_case.

title: No late-arrival, freeze or replay rule on any fact table
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Reporting and Analytics Data Model v3.xlsx
description: The grains are written as one row per open case per day, per decision, per treatment, per receipt and per bucket per month, but the model carries no business date, no as-of rule, no statement of what happens when an event arrives after the cut-off and no way to rebuild a day. In the target the events arrive at any hour and the same business date can be republished.
evidence: v3 Facts!B5 to B13 (grains only); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 lines 2936 and 2968 (each producer writes to its outbox in the same transaction; consumers dedupe through their inbox table) and line 2327 (rerun any business date); LDM v8 fields DF-RPT-041 to DF-RPT-052 (business_date, is_baseline, frozen, published_at) and DF-RPT-056 to DF-RPT-058 (the publish counts and held_reason); DP-09.
proposed: Each row of the Read model sheet carries the inbox dedupe, the business-date order, the reopen-until-frozen rule and the rebuild from the retained topic history.

title: dim_org holds an owner while events carry no personal data
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Reporting and Analytics Data Model v3.xlsx
description: dim_org is defined as Team, region, queue and owner, with history, and fact_case_daily carries owner and team as dimensions. In the target the read model is fed from events that carry IDs and facts, never personal data, so an owner name in a dashboard fact needs either an ID-only rule or a masking rule, and version 3 states neither.
evidence: v3 Dimensions!B9 (Team, region, queue and owner, with history); v3 Facts!C5 (owner, team, queue as dimensions); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 line 2936 and line 2968 (events carry IDs and facts, never personal data); Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables rows queue_member and assignment (P3) and masking_rule (P4); Template and Rules R7.2 s17 guardrails (no PII in events, workflow inputs or logs).
proposed: The read model keys the owner and the team by ID from the events and resolves the display name from the P3 queue_member and assignment rows behind the rwb-access masking policy; no personal data travels on an event.

title: The LDM and the FSD still publish to Power BI, which is removed
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Reporting and Analytics Data Model v3.xlsx
description: The reporting model under this document is the source of the case list and queue measures that the LDM v8 and FSD P3 describe as published to Power BI, while Arch v5 removes the Power BI feed (INT-19) and serves the steering dashboard and the reports from rwb-reporting. Two documents of the set therefore still name a consumer that no longer exists, and this data model is the one that must say what replaces it.
evidence: Recovery Workbench Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 entities case_list_row (One row of the daily case list per case account and business date, published to Power BI) and queue_measure (One snapshot of a queue counts, ageing and breaches, published when it reconciles to the case list); FSD P3 v4 FEAT-CWC-18 (publishes queue measures to the case list and Power BI); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 lines 664 to 665 (Data lake / Power BI not connected, INT-19/20 removed) and lines 2701 to 2703 (Removed: reports from rwb-reporting); ADR-018; DP-17.
proposed: The read model serves the dashboards and the reports through GET /dashboards/{id} and GET /reports/{id}; the Power BI wording in LDM v8 and FSD P3 is read as consumed through rwb-reporting and is corrected in those documents, not here.
